name: Alphabet
target_note: Targets being cut after the report (18 of 21 analysts)
why_fell: Search revenue missed ($63.35B vs about $64.96B expected) and free cash flow turned negative (−$9.07B) on heavy AI spending. Its worst day since the 2004 IPO.
bull: Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7B, and the shares trade near 15× earnings, the cheapest in years.
bear: If AI is eating into search, the core profit engine shrinks. Spending is partly funded with debt and share sales.
trigger: Holds above the $270.70 52-week low and closes higher for a few sessions.

name: Meta Platforms
why_fell: Third-quarter capex ($34.9B) outran operating cash flow, so free cash flow turned negative; it plans up to $97.5B of new stock and paused buybacks.
bull: Revenue grew 26% to $64.6B with a $73–76B fourth-quarter outlook; about 19× forward earnings against a 21× five-year average.
bear: Heavy dilution, no 2027 revenue outlook, and 2027 capex expected near $203B.
trigger: A steady base, and any sign spending is levelling off. The next big read is the late-January report.

name: Nvidia
why_fell: Sold with the chip sector after Intel's weak outlook, as cloud giants' cash strain raises doubts about AI-chip demand.
bull: Data-center revenue grew 117% last quarter and analysts are nearly all bullish.
bear: Below its 50-day average with lower highs all month; it falls harder than the market in sell-offs.

name: Amazon
why_fell: Missed on earnings and revenue; capex of $77.3B and record free-cash outflow. Down about 2.5% Friday after trimming a 7% premarket loss.
bull: AWS grew 39%, its fastest in nearly five years; management sees AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028.
bear: Free cash flow is negative and spending rises again in 2027.
trigger: Rebuilds above the $240 area it just lost.

name: Fortinet
why_fell: Beat on earnings ($0.91 vs $0.85) and sales, but cut its full-year service-revenue outlook, hinting customers add fewer services.
bull: Billings up 29% and revenue up 20%; management calls the service gap timing and added $1.2B to buybacks.
bear: Analysts cut targets and BofA downgraded; the stock had already run up 62% this year.
trigger: A few calm sessions above Thursday's low before looking again.

name: Advanced Micro Devices
why_fell: Fell about 12% in the chip sell-off triggered by Intel's weak PC outlook, days before its own Nov 3 report.
bull: A leading AI-chip maker; Wall Street still sees upside.
bear: Shares had more than doubled this year, so the bar for Nov 3 is high.
trigger: Wait for the Nov 3 results and the market's reaction.

name: Illumina
why_fell: Revenue of $1.13B missed by about $20M and organic growth stayed near 4%, though adjusted EPS beat ($1.44 vs $1.36).
bull: Raised its full-year revenue outlook to $4.64–4.66B.
bear: It traded near 49× forward earnings before the drop, a price that assumed much faster growth.
trigger: Evidence that organic growth is speeding up.

name: Intel
why_fell: Third quarter beat, but the fourth-quarter outlook missed on a severe PC slump and a factory accident in Israel.
bull: Earnings came in above forecasts ($0.52 vs $0.40).
bear: A near-30% one-day collapse; Wall Street is cautious on execution.
trigger: Selling has to dry up first. No setup yet.

name: SanDisk
why_fell: Sold with the chip sector after Intel's outlook; no company-specific news reported.
bull: The fall looks tied to the sector rout rather than its own results.
bear: Memory stocks swing hard, and the shares had climbed to very high levels.
trigger: Chip stocks stabilise and it holds above Friday's close.
